# iliad-152 (Iliad 24.1–92) — review, pass 1 (units.json, new-renderings.md) and pass 2 (gloss.json)

Method, pass 1: every grammatical label in every note checked against the form and the line in the packet; every positional claim (“begins/ends in the middle of line N”, “in 54”, “in 92”, “from the next line”) checked against the packet lines; cross-references checked (1.493 = iliad-005 unit at 493; 8.409 = iliad-050 unit at 409; 4.48–49 = iliad-021 unit at 48, spoken by Zeus; ἔτλητε in 35 / τλητόν in 49; ὁμὴν τιμήν in 57; ἅλιαι in 84 / ἅλιον in 92; speech ranges 33–54, 56–63, 65–76, 88, 90–92); each unit read Greek to `l` word by word, then `l` against `i`, then `i` for remembered English (none recalled; “What you say might stand” at 56 was the one phrase that arrived fully formed and decided what the Greek leaves open, see below); quotation marks and `mark` (neighbour: the last unit of /home/user/Lectorium/iliad-151.json, 896–897, ends narration without an open quote, so line 1 opens outside any speech; openers at 33, 56, 65, 88, 90 each carry “ in `l` and `i` and a `mark`; closers at 54, 62, 75, 88, 92 carry ” in both layers; every speech opened is closed inside the part); the three whole-line/whole-unit repeats (24.64 = iliad-006 at 560, 24.87 = iliad-015 at 790, 24.31’s first line = iliad-005 at 493) compared exactly; the 4.48–49 reuse at 68–70 compared exactly with the published unit (l and i of the two lines identical apart from the closing ” the published speech-end carries); 24.77’s first line compared with iliad-050 at 409; 24.8 compared with odyssey-034; every epithet and formula grepped in both conventions files (house-renderings tables). Line 6 hand-scanned (below). `t` untouched (checked by script after every edit: all 71 `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p`, `mark`, title, titleEn, part and about identical to the drafter’s file except the fields listed). Counts, units: high 1, medium 17, low 11 (unit numbers are the unit’s first line `ln`). Counts, gloss: high 0, medium 1, low 3.

## Line 6 (flagged: UNRESOLVED; closed syllable scanned short: ἀνδροτῆτά)

Hand scan of Πατρόκλου ποθέων ἀνδροτῆτά τε καὶ μένος ἠΰ: Πα-τρό (– –, both long by position) | κλου πο-θέ (– ⏑ ⏑, θέων one syllable by synizesis) | ων ἀν-δρο (– ⏑ ⏑) | τῆ-τά τε (– ⏑ ⏑) | καὶ μέ-νος (– ⏑ ⏑) | ἠ-ΰ (– ×). Sixteen syllables; the only way to the pattern is to scan ἀν- short although the ν closes it and the next syllable begins with a cluster. The irregularity is real (the word is one that the metre fits only with a short first syllable), the drafter’s note already says so in one sentence at the right unit (line 5, which holds line 6), and that sentence was true except for “closed by ν and δ”: only ν closes the syllable. Corrected.

## Changes (new-renderings.md)

Rows rewritten to match the units above: ἀεικείην; κτέρεα κτερίσαιεν; βίῃ καὶ ἀγήνορι θυμῷ; ἦτορ ἀπηύρα (i “has taken the life from”, as the unit has it); τὸν δὲ χολωσαμένη …; εἴη κεν καὶ τοῦτο τεὸν ἔπος; κακῶν ἕταρ’, αἰὲν ἄπιστε; λάθρῃ Ἀχιλλῆος (steal, not take); ἀλλ’ εἴ τις καλέσειε …; ἐπεστονάχησε δὲ λίμνη; ἀγραύλοιο βοὸς κέρας. No row contradicted a table row after these; the existing rows were checked against the tables (ἄγριος 7.206, ἀπήχθετο 6.140, ἄτη, νεικέω, σχέτλιος, ὀλοός “deadly” 12.425 of the Odyssey, ἐναίσιμος, νεμεσσάω, ἄφθιτος, ἄκριτα, ποθέω, μένος ἠΰ, θῖν’ ἁλός, κνίση, ἐΐσης, δυωδεκάτη, μέσσαυλον, κλισίη, σῆμα, ὠμησταί, ἀργεϊφόντης, ἐύσκοπος, ἀργυρόπεζα) and agree.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json (109 entries: the 108 novel forms plus “__broaden__”)

Every novel form’s parse checked against every line it stands in (the packet lines), the known-form entries spot-checked for coverage of the uses in this part (τὸν, τὴν, τοὶ/τοί, ὃς/ὅς/ἣ/ἥ, ᾧ/ᾗ/οὗ, οἱ, ὦρτο, ὄρουσεν, ἔμελλε, εἴη, εἴπῃ, κεν, ἔστι, ἵνα, ὄφρά, περὶ, ἀμφὶ, ἐνὶ, κατὰ, ὑφ’, ἕκαστοι, κῆρι, ἠώς, ἀποδρύφοι and others: all covered, and the glosser’s 17 broadenings are true of their lines). After my edits to units.json it was re-read from disk and the entries compared again with the revised English.

## Considered and refused

- τολύπευσε: i “had carried through” against the Odyssey table’s i “wound up” (14.368, of a war). The table’s English is for a war; here the object is ὁπόσα “all that”, `l` keeps “wound up” and the note explains the image; “wound up all that he had” would not be English. Kept, with the drafter’s row.
- i “Priam and his people” (line 28) for λαός: the Greek has no possessive; the part’s own sense (Priam’s people) and the note’s “people” make it the natural reading. Kept.
- ἔτλητε: l “have not endured”, i “could not … bring yourselves”: the drafter’s row records this as deliberate; l is literal. Kept.
- μενεαίνων “in eagerness”: follows the table exactly (4.32, 16.491, 19.367); the note’s remark that the anger is for the reader to supply is the table’s own reasoning. Kept.
- ἄκριτα l “unsorted”, i “endless”: exactly the table (3.412). Kept.
- ἀείκιζεν gloss “treat shamefully, outrage” while the house English is “ill-treated”: glosses carry the lexical sense, not the house rendering. Kept.
- μήν gloss “(= epic μέν)”: LSJ’s own equation; unusual to read but not wrong. Kept.
- Ποσειδάων’: the note says only that it is elided and construed as Ἥρῃ is; true whichever case is restored. Kept.
- ἄλλοτε/ἠέ/ἤτοι and the other known particles: covered by existing entries.
- ἀτίτηλα’s “aorist 1 sg.”: right.
- Not run: validate_iliad.py (needs the built part and iliad-152.json, which does not exist yet); nothing in this review depends on it, but the whole-unit repeat checks it would make (24.64, 24.87) were done by hand and match.
